# haul

> A command-line video and audio downloader for YouTube, X, bilibili, Xiaoyuzhou and Apple Podcasts, as one binary for macOS, Linux and Windows. Built to be driven by AI agents: `--json` output, no prompts without a terminal, meaningful exit codes.

## Quick start

1. Inspect: `haul info --json "<url>"`. One page: its video and audio streams (each with an `index`) and every subtitle track (machine-generated ones marked `auto: true`). Several pages (playlist, season, show, multi-video post): the list of pages only; add `-p <n>` for a page's streams.
2. Download: `haul --json "<url>"` takes the best streams. To choose, either pass the `index` values from step 1 with `--video-stream N --audio-stream N`, or give priorities: `-q 720p -c avc,m4a`.
3. Read stdout: check `ok`, then top-level `files`, the absolute paths of the output files, whether just written or already there from an earlier run. Per page: `pages[].status`, `pages[].file`, `pages[].extraFiles`.

With `--json`, stdout carries exactly one JSON document and nothing else; progress and logs go to stderr. Do not parse stderr. Never build output paths yourself: take them from the JSON. In a pipeline (`haul … | jq`) the exit code is lost unless you `set -o pipefail`, but `ok` says the same thing.

```sh
haul --json -w ~/Downloads "<url>" 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'if .ok then .files[] else "error: " + .error.message end'
```

## Rules

- Quote URLs: they contain `?` and `&`.
- Never pass `-i` / `--interactive`: it needs a terminal and fails with exit code 2 without one.
- Stream indexes are 0-based and follow haul's sort order, which `-q`, `-c`, `--video-ascending` and `--audio-ascending` change. Pass the same ordering flags to `info` and to the download, or use indexes from a plain `info` with no ordering flags at all.
- Pages are 1-based, as `info` numbers them. `-p` takes `3`, `1-5`, `1,4`, `ALL`, `LAST`. `LAST` (also `LATEST`) is the last page, which is the newest episode of a podcast show (shows are listed oldest first). Without `-p`, a link to one episode or `?p=N` takes that page; otherwise a download takes all pages.
- Where files go: the current directory, or `-w <dir>`. An item with one page is saved as `<title>.<ext>`. An item with several pages is saved in a folder named after it, as `<title>/[P<n>]<pageTitle>.<ext>`, even when `-p` picks one page; `<n>` is zero-padded to the page count (`P003` of 155). Change this with `-o` (one page) and `--multi-output` (several); `haul templates` lists the variables. Don't include an extension; haul adds it.
- By default the output file, audio-only files included, also contains the subtitles (not auto-generated ones), chapters, the cover (as an attached picture, which ffprobe shows as a `video` stream) and tags. `--skip-subtitle` and `--skip-cover` leave them out, for example for a pure audio file. `--sub-lang en,zh` keeps only those languages; a prefix matches (`zh` takes `zh-CN`, `en` takes `en-US`). `--auto-subtitles` adds machine-generated ones (for some bilibili videos they are the only subtitles there are). Inside the file, languages are tagged with ISO 639-2 codes (`chi`, `eng`).
- Re-running is safe. A page whose output file exists is reported as `"status": "skipped", "reason": "exists"` and is not downloaded again.
- Smallest download: `--video-ascending --audio-ascending` (lowest quality and smallest streams first; each flag orders one kind). `-q 360P` alone still takes the best audio.
- Audio only: `--audio-only` gives `.m4a` with the best audio stream, which may be Opus. Add `-c m4a` to prefer AAC. Podcasts keep `.mp3` / `.m4a`.
- `-q` and `-c` are priorities, not filters: when nothing matches, haul takes the next best. Check what was used: `video[selectedVideo]` and `audio[selectedAudio]`.
- Subtitles only: `--subtitle-only` writes `<name>.<lang>.srt` files (`<name>.<lang>.auto.srt` for machine-generated ones). They appear in `extraFiles` and `files`; `file` is absent. When there is nothing to save, the page is `"status": "skipped", "reason": "empty"`. Cover only: `--cover-only`.
- bilibili danmaku: `--danmaku` adds them next to the video, `--danmaku-only` writes only them; `--danmaku-format ass` (or `xml`) limits the files, default both.
- Stream URLs: `haul info --json --urls "<url>"` adds each stream's `url`. They expire quickly and some need the site's headers, so prefer letting haul download.

## Exit codes and errors

| code | error.kind | meaning | what to do |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | – | done | read `files` / `pages[]` |
| 1 | failed | network, site or muxing failure | retry later; add `--debug` for detail |
| 2 | input | unsupported link, bad `-p`, stream index out of range | fix the input; `haul --help` lists the link forms |
| 3 | dependency | ffmpeg / yt-dlp missing | install it; the message says how on this system |
| 4 | auth | login needed or expired | a person runs `haul login bilibili` |
| 64 | – | unknown flag or missing argument (plain text on stderr, no JSON) | check `haul download --help` |
| 130 | cancelled | cancelled | – |

On failure, stdout still has one JSON document: `"ok": false` and `"error": {"kind", "message", "exitCode"}`. If the item was already read, it also has `title`, `pages` and the other fields, including the pages finished before the error. If the link could not be read, only `ok`, `command`, `input`, `files` (empty) and `error` are present, so guard against a missing `pages`.

## Sites

- **YouTube**: `youtube.com/watch?v=…`, `youtu.be/…`, `/shorts/…`, `/embed/…`, `/live/…`. Needs yt-dlp and deno. Qualities `1080p`, `720p60`… Video codecs `AV1`, `VP9`, `AVC`; audio `M4A` (AAC), `OPUS`. `-c avc,m4a` gives files that QuickTime plays.
- **X**: `x.com/<user>/status/<id>` or `twitter.com/…`; `…/video/<n>` takes one video of a post. Needs yt-dlp. Each video stream already includes the audio (`videoHasAudio: true`, `hasAudio: true`, no `audio`); the codec may show as `MP4`. A post with several videos has one page per video.
- **bilibili**: `bilibili.com/video/BV…`, bangumi, courses, collections, favorites, user spaces, `b23.tv/…`, or a bare `BV…` / `av…` / `ep…` / `ss…`. Logged out, it offers only lower qualities, typically up to 480P (`"loggedIn": false`); 1080P and above need `haul login bilibili`. Qualities `8K`, `Dolby Vision`, `HDR`, `4K`, `1080P60`, `1080P+`, `1080P`, `720P`, `480P`, `360P`. Codecs `AV1`, `HEVC`, `AVC`. `--danmaku` saves the bullet comments.
- **Xiaoyuzhou**: `xiaoyuzhoufm.com/episode/<id>`, `/podcast/<id>`. A show page lists only its latest episodes.
- **Apple Podcasts**: `podcasts.apple.com/<cc>/podcast/<name>/id<show>?i=<episode>`, or without `?i=` for the whole show. Apple returns only a show's recent episodes, so `pageCount` can be well below the real total; download older episodes by their episode link.

`-q` and `-c` match case-insensitively. Codec names in the JSON are upper case.

## JSON document

`?` marks a field that can be missing: keys are left out when there is no value. Keys come out sorted.

```
ok: bool          command: "download" | "info"          input: string
site: "youtube" | "x" | "bilibili" | "xiaoyuzhou" | "applePodcasts"
title, uploader?, published? (ISO 8601, UTC), description?, loggedIn? (bilibili only), pageCount
files: [absolute path]          output files of the pages taken, new or skipped; [] for info
error?: { kind, message, exitCode }
pages[]: {                      every page of the item, selected or not
  index (1-based, what -p takes), id, title, durationSeconds?,
  selected                      the run took this page (info without -p on a list takes none)
  published?                    the page's own date where the site has one (episodes, list items);
                                the parts of one bilibili video share the video's date
  status?: "listed" | "downloaded" | "skipped"      absent on pages the run did not take
  reason?: "exists" | "archive" | "no-mux" | "empty"
  file? (absolute), sizeBytes?, extraFiles? (absolute: subtitles, danmaku, a cover, unmuxed streams)
  video?: [{ index (0-based), quality?, resolution?, codec, fps?, bitrateKbps?, sizeBytes?, hasAudio?, url? }]
  audio?: [{ index (0-based), codec, bitrateKbps?, sizeBytes?, url? }]
  videoHasAudio?, selectedVideo?, selectedAudio?
  subtitles?: [{ lang (BCP 47, e.g. en, zh-CN), auto? }]
}
```

`sizeBytes` on a stream is the site's figure or an estimate from bitrate × duration. `pages[].sizeBytes` is the real size of the file written.

## More

- `haul --help`: sites, agent usage, exit codes, examples
- `haul download --help`: every option (`--help-hidden` adds bilibili network options)
- `haul templates`: file-name template variables
- Config defaults: `~/.config/haul/config.json`, with option names in camelCase and bilibili's under `"bilibili"` (e.g. `{"subLang": "en", "bilibili": {"api": "tv"}}`)
